title: Congenital Hyperinsulinism of Infancy: ABCC8 Genetics, 18F-DOPA and Diazoxide
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology

steps.say: Drawing laboratory studies at the immediate nadir of blood glucose captures inappropriately active anabolism.
steps.tx: Document endogenous hyperinsulinemic drive through immediate **Critical sample diagnostic hormone benchmarks** during hypoglycemia. During spontaneous hypoglycemia (plasma glucose < 50 mg/dL), a critical blood sample confirms hyperinsulinism: detectable serum insulin (> 2-3 microU/mL), suppressed beta-hydroxybutyrate (< 1.8 mmol/L), and absent free fatty acids.

vis.alt: Medical illustration of acute hypoglycaemia depicting neuroglycopenic manifestations and autonomic counterregulatory response.
vis.caption: Neuroglycopenic cascade and autonomic counterregulatory hormonal failure in severe infant hypoglycaemia.

steps.say: Intravenous or intramuscular glucagon challenge tests liver glycogen mobilization during severe neuroglycopenia.
steps.tx: Confirm inappropriate glycogen preservation through the **Glucagon stimulation test glycemic response** at hypoglycemia nadir. Intramuscular or IV glucagon (1 mg or 0.03 mg/kg) given at the nadir of hypoglycemia triggers an exaggerated glucose rise >= 30 mg/dL within 40 minutes, pathognomonic of inappropriately preserved liver glycogen stores.

nodes.label: Exaggerated Glucose Rise >= 30 mg/dL in 40 Minutes

steps.say: Loss of function mutations within potassium channel subunits cause uninterrupted beta cell depolarization.
steps.tx: Investigate channelopathy molecular mechanisms analyzing **K_ATP channel molecular genetics (ABCC8 and KCNJ11)** on chromosome 11. Loss-of-function mutations in ABCC8 (SUR1) and KCNJ11 (Kir6.2) on chromosome 11p15.1 impair K_ATP channel closure, causing continuous beta-cell membrane depolarization and unsuppressed calcium-driven exocytosis of insulin.

steps.say: Potassium channel opening agents represent the standard first line pharmacotherapy for persistent hyperinsulinism.
steps.tx: Restore membrane polarization through pharmacologic management initiating **Diazoxide first-line medical therapy** in neonates. Diazoxide (5-15 mg/kg/day divided TID) is the first-line K_ATP channel opener; co-administration with chlorothiazide (7-10 mg/kg/day) is mandatory to prevent fluid retention, pulmonary hypertension, and cardiac failure.

nodes.label: Prevents Severe Fluid Retention & Pulmonary Hypertension

steps.say: Differentiation between focal adenomatous lesions and generalized pancreatic involvement governs surgical strategy.
steps.tx: Distinguish distinct structural and genetic variants comparing **Focal vs diffuse histological forms** of hyperinsulinism. Diffuse hyperinsulinism affects the entire pancreas (autosomal recessive/dominant), while focal hyperinsulinism is caused by a paternal ABCC8 mutation combined with somatic maternal 11p15 loss of heterozygosity in a localized adenomatous cluster.

left.title: Diffuse Hyperinsulinism
points: Affects every beta cell across entire pancreas

right.title: Focal Hyperinsulinism
points: Localized adenomatous cluster of beta cells

steps.say: Positron emission tomography utilizing radiofluorinated dopamine precursors accurately identifies focal lesions.
steps.tx: Map focal lesions preoperatively by utilizing **18F-fluoro-L-DOPA PET-CT scan gold standard** molecular imaging. 18F-DOPA PET-CT accurately discriminates focal from diffuse disease with > 95% sensitivity and pinpoints the anatomical location of the focal lesion for curative partial surgical resection. This avoids extensive pancreatic tissue loss.

vis.title: 18F-DOPA PET-CT Diagnostic Accuracy
rows: Accurately separates focal from diffuse forms
Guides targeted laparoscopic or open lesionectomy

steps.tx: Surgery for hyperinsulinism depends on knowing whether one spot or the whole gland misbehaves. Pancreatic islet cells take up the tracer, and a **focal 18F-DOPA** hot spot on PET marks a small cluster of overactive tissue that a limited resection can cure. Diffuse uptake instead spreads through the gland, warning the surgeon that removing one segment will not control the hypoglycaemia.
steps.say: A single intense 18F-DOPA hot spot marks focal disease that limited resection can cure. Uptake spread through the pancreas points to diffuse disease instead.

vis.alt: PET scan of the pancreas with one intense focal hot spot of tracer uptake standing out from faint background activity.
vis.caption: PET image showing focal pancreatic 18F-DOPA uptake in congenital hyperinsulinism. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Somatostatin receptor agonists suppress insulin exocytosis downstream of defective potassium channel architecture.
steps.tx: Manage diazoxide-refractory neonates using second-line agents through **Octreotide and somatostatin analogs** administration. In diazoxide-unresponsive patients, subcutaneous octreotide (5-30 mcg/kg/day divided QID or continuous SC) inhibits insulin release via somatostatin receptor 5 (SSTR5); monitor for tachyphylaxis and necrotizing enterocolitis in neonates.

steps.say: Near total resection carries inevitable long term endocrine and exocrine functional failure in children.
steps.tx: Evaluate definitive surgical salvage in diffuse refractory disease through **Subtotal pancreatectomy in refractory diffuse disease** procedures. Severe diffuse K_ATP hyperinsulinism refractory to medical therapies requires 95-98% near-total pancreatectomy, carrying a 90% long-term risk of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and exocrine insufficiency.

vis.title: Outcomes of Near-Total Pancreatectomy
rows: Spares rim of tissue along duodenal loop
